clue.text: Carry on to back of leaf-there's several to prune out

definitions.text: Carry on to back of leaf

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener is told there are several shoots to cut back on a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal: SEVERAL TO PRUNE rearranges into the fourteen letters. The phrase is the note printed at the foot of a page telling a reader to continue overleaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the instruction at the bottom of a printed page telling the reader the text continues on the reverse.

clue.text: Reduce cover, not capital

parts.note: to reduce something is to lower it
a case is a protective cover

explanation.surface: A cut in protective covering is described as not a big deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money or a city, but here it means a capital letter; small letters are the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters, as opposed to capitals, are named after the lower tray of type in old printing.

clue.text: Deep hole -one near ship

parts.note: a means one
by means near, as in standing by the door
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A deep hole lies close to a vessel at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasm or bottomless pit, a deep hole in the earth or sea floor.

clue.text: Unconventionally scale a rocky peak using powered conveyor

indicators.note: doing something unconventionally means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A climber scales a peak in an odd way, with mechanical help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconventionally' rearranges SCALE into ESCAL; 'using' only links. A tor is a rocky hilltop, a word common on English moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase, a motor-driven belt of steps carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Starts to uncover peccadillos for every superior

indicators.note: the starts of the next two words are their opening letters

parts.note: per means for every, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A disgraced figure's small sins are exposed one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: Higher in position or rank, as an upper class or upper floor is above the rest.

clue.text: Fruit drink in Egypt

parts.note: nectar is the drink of the gods, or a sweet juice
taken as written
ET is the code for Egypt, but E is used here as an abbreviation for the country

explanation.surface: Someone orders fruit juice while on holiday in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Fiddle with flower girl in Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: Someone plays a stringed instrument with a flower girl in a Shakespeare comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a stringed instrument (loosely a fiddle), a small pansy-like flower, and the heroine of Shakespeare's comedy Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a bowed instrument a little larger than a violin, a garden pansy, and Shakespeare's shipwrecked heroine who dresses as a boy.

clue.text: Favour wild otters on tip of estuary

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tip of the word estuary is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wild otters play at the mouth of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges OTTERS into ROSETT; 'tip of' adds the E of estuary. 'Favour' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour can be a ribbon or badge worn to show support, such as a rosette for a party or team.

clue.text: Get in wrecked boat first

indicators.note: first says the wrecked boat comes ahead of the other piece
a wrecked boat is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tries to board a boat that has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get in' reads as climbing aboard, but 'in' is a piece; 'wrecked' gives OBTA from the boat and 'first' sets it in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire or come by something.

clue.text: Incidentally, leave out the side road

indicators.note: to leave out a word is to remove it

parts.note: by the way is a phrase meaning incidentally
taken as written

explanation.surface: In passing, a driver is told to avoid the minor road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incidentally' gives BY THE WAY; 'leave out the' takes out THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor or little-used road off the main route.

clue.text: Better to take current debts as sizeable

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
AC is alternating current
IOUs are written promises to pay, so debts

explanation.surface: A gambler bets more, taking on large debts at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb meaning to top; 'to take' and 'as' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy and large, able to hold a great deal.

clue.text: Arranged a looser spray

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Flowers are arranged in a looser spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges LOOSER into EROSOL. 'spray' looks like a bunch of flowers that has been arranged, but it is a can of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can that releases its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: Go through text of one exercise to modify again

parts.note: to read is to go through a text
a means one
PT stands for physical training

explanation.surface: A student reads one exercise and revises it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust or adapt something once more.

clue.text: Gets close to new listeners

parts.note: ears are the organs we listen with

explanation.surface: A newcomer approaches an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaches, comes nearer.

clue.text: Subordinate has to notify it in rough sea

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another
a rough sea is churned up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to tell someone is to notify them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A junior officer must report something during a storm at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges the sea into SAE, and 'in' sets the telling between its S A and E; 'has' only links. 'Subordinate' is a noun here, a dependent.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite state or person is one dependent on and controlled by a more powerful one.

clue.text: Conclude animal fur (not tail) is in gallery

indicators.note: is in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: not tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat

explanation.surface: A gallery exhibit of animal fur without its tail is finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not tail' drops the last E of the fur, giving ERMIN, and 'is in' puts that inside the Tate, a famous London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or bring to a close.

clue.text: Fats in the ranks? That's disorderly behaviour

indicators.note: in says one piece is put inside another

parts.note: ranks are rows, as of seats or soldiers
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Soldiers eating in their lines cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Fats', an OCR slip for 'Eats'. 'in' puts the eating inside the ranks; 'That's' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy, rough conduct, the quality of being boisterous.

clue.text: After a season's growth fed der store goes up in Greek citadel

indicators.note: After puts the turned store behind the other pieces

parts.note: a crop is what grows in a season

indicators.note: goes up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a silo stores fodder for livestock

explanation.surface: A farmer's silo is raised once the harvest is in.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'fed der', an OCR split of 'fodder'. In a down clue 'goes up' reads the store backwards as OLIS, and 'After' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified high part of an ancient Greek city, most famously at Athens.

clue.text: Bring down ball that's gone too far

explanation.surface: A rebel ousts the leader with a wild throw.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an overthrow is a fielder's return that misses the stumps and runs on, allowing extra runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a government by force, and in cricket a wild return from the field that lets batsmen take extra runs.

clue.text: Best work — it uplifted parent

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
mum is a parent

explanation.surface: A child shows a parent their best piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifted' reads the pronoun upwards, giving TI. 'Best' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: The most favourable or ideal condition or amount.

clue.text: Bird to feel sorry for losing its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to regret is to feel sorry

explanation.surface: Someone pities a bird that has been decapitated.
explanation.definitionFit: A white heron with long plumes.

clue.text: Difficult score in Rugby centre?

parts.note: a try is a score in rugby
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Scoring at the heart of a rugby match is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby centre' reads as a player position, but it gives G, the middle letter of RUGBY.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard to bear or deal with, annoyingly testing.

clue.text: Deals with rigging on forepart of ship

parts.note: tackle is the ropes and pulleys of a ship's rigging

indicators.note: the forepart of the word ship is its first letter

explanation.surface: A sailor works with the ropes at the bow of a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Copes with or confronts a problem.

clue.text: Officer's brief regarding punctuation

parts.note: Col is the short form of colonel, an officer
on means regarding, about

explanation.surface: A commanding officer's short report concerns punctuation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a written briefing, but it signals the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-dot mark used to introduce a list or explanation.

clue.text: Some of the girls quibble about throwing firework

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few girls argue over a firework being thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'girls' into 'quibble'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small firework, often thrown, that hisses before exploding.

clue.text: To respond legally in the matter of exercise

parts.note: in re is the Latin legal phrase for in the matter of
to ply is to exercise or use, as in plying a trade

explanation.surface: A lawyer must answer on the subject of a fitness regime.
explanation.walkthrough: IN RE is Latin used in legal headings and letters to mean 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a response or answer, in the manner of a rejoinder.

clue.text: Moved higher, lifting title by two points

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Sir is a title
E and N are two compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Someone is raised to a knighthood with a couple of extra points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' turns SIR into RIS; 'by' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone up, ascended.

clue.text: Large number — 1,000 last month -due it originally

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
ult., short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

indicators.note: originally hints the letters were in another order before, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds from last month is now owing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' rearranges DUE IT into ITUDE. ULT (ultimo) is an old commercial abbreviation for last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A great crowd or host of people or things.

clue.text: Sale (25% off) operating in hairdresser's shop

indicators.note: a quarter off a four-letter word keeps its first three letters, cutting the last

parts.note: on means operating, switched on

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's runs a quarter-off sale.
explanation.walkthrough: '25% off' keeps three of the four letters of SALE, dropping the E; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair or beauty parlour is called a salon.

clue.text: Primate calling for dishonest behaviour

parts.note: a monkey is a primate
a calling is one's trade or business

explanation.surface: An ape's cry is described as roguery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like the cry of the primate, but it means a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief or underhand trickery.
